name: Elamipretide (SS-31)

track.title: Pilot in people
track.line: Small studies in heart, muscle and eye disease

track.title: Phase II
track.line: Phase 2 trials in heart, eye and muscle disease

what.text: Elamipretide is a short peptide of 4 amino acids: D-Arg-2,6-dimethyl-Tyr-Lys-Phe-NH2. The arginine is in its mirror-image (D) form. The medicine contains it as a hydrochloride salt. It is also known by its research code SS-31 and the older code MTP-131.

Its maker is Stealth BioTherapeutics. It is sold as Forzinity, an injection under the skin, approved by FDA in September 2025 for Barth syndrome, a rare inherited mitochondrial disease that mainly affects males.

src.label: FDA news release, accelerated approval of Forzinity

items.text: The label calls it a mitochondrial cardiolipin binder. It settles in the inner membrane of mitochondria, the energy-producing parts of cells, and the label says it improves their shape and function.
After an injection under the skin, blood levels peak within 30 to 60 minutes, and about 92% of the dose reaches the blood.

what.text: The approval covers Barth syndrome only. Use for ageing or longevity would be off-label, and no trial has tested elamipretide for longevity.

research.text: Human evidence: one tiny approval trial in Barth syndrome that missed its main goals, with muscle strength gains seen later in an open-label extension. Larger trials in other diseases mostly missed their main goals. One small study in older adults measured muscle energy after a single infusion.

research.title: Barth syndrome (TAZPOWER), the basis for approval

facts.v: NCT03098797, sponsored by Stealth BioTherapeutics
randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover, then a 168-week open-label extension
12 males aged 12 to 35 with genetically confirmed Barth syndrome; 11 were white
12 weeks on elamipretide and 12 weeks on placebo, with 4 weeks off between; 8 people stayed on through week 168
40 mg under the skin once a day
main goals: 6-minute walk distance and a fatigue score. Knee muscle strength was a secondary measure.

research.found: Elamipretide was not better than placebo on either main goal. Knee strength did not rise in the randomized part. It rose during the open-label extension, where everyone got the drug and there was no placebo group. FDA based the accelerated approval on that knee strength change.

research.title: Primary mitochondrial myopathy (MMPOWER-3)

facts.v: Karaa A, et al. Neurology 2023;101(3):e238-52; NCT03323749
randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled
218 adults with genetic mitochondrial muscle disease; mean age 45.6, 64% women
24 weeks
40 mg under the skin once a day, or placebo
6-minute walk distance and a fatigue score

research.found: The trial did not meet its main goals. Walk distance differed from placebo by −3.2 meters, and fatigue scores did not differ. The open-label part was stopped for this reason. Most side effects were mild to moderate.

research.title: Dry age-related macular degeneration (ReCLAIM-2)

facts.v: NCT03891875; Ophthalmology Science 2024
randomized, double-masked, placebo-controlled
176 people aged 55 or older with geographic atrophy (117 elamipretide, 59 placebo)
48 weeks
40 mg under the skin once a day, or placebo
vision in low light and growth of the atrophy area

research.found: It missed both main goals. Some secondary eye-scan measures differed from placebo, which the authors report with nominal P values. Side effects were reported in 86% on elamipretide and 71% on placebo, mostly injection site reactions.

research.title: One infusion in older adults with weak muscle mitochondria

facts.v: Roshanravan B, et al. PLoS One 2021;16(7):e0253849; NCT02245620
randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled
39 healthy adults aged 60 to 85 with poorly working muscle mitochondria; 46% women
a single infusion into a vein over 2 hours, 0.25 mg/kg each hour
maximum ATP (energy) production in a hand muscle, and hand muscle fatigue

research.found: Right after the infusion, ATP production was higher than with placebo (P = 0.055 for the change; P = 0.045 for the percent change). There was no difference on day 7, and no difference in muscle fatigue. Stealth funded the study, and three authors were paid consultants for Stealth from 2014 to 2016.

research.title: Heart attack treated with stenting (EMBRACE STEMI)

facts.v: NCT01572909, sponsored by Stealth BioTherapeutics
randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled
300 adults with a first front-wall heart attack
an infusion into a vein starting before the artery was opened
heart muscle damage, by the amount of the enzyme CK-MB released over 72 hours

research.found: Average CK-MB release was similar in both groups (6,582 against 6,738 units). The registry posts no statistical test.

research.text: Registered trials with no results yet

items.text: an open-label Phase 2a pilot in about 30 healthy adults aged 65 to 80, given injections under the skin once a day for 4 weeks, sponsored by David Marcinek. The main measure is side effects. Recruiting since November 2025; no results posted.
the confirmatory trial FDA required. Phase 3b/4, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, about 48 males aged 5 to 55, 72 weeks. Recruiting since July 2026; completion estimated November 2029.
Phase 3 in dry macular degeneration, 313 people enrolled, 96 weeks. Primary completion estimated August 2027.
Phase 3, 48 weeks, 102 adults with mitochondrial muscle disease due to nuclear DNA changes. Completed December 2024; no results posted.

us.text: FDA-approved as Forzinity under accelerated approval, on September 19, 2025, to improve muscle strength in adults and children with Barth syndrome who weigh at least 30 kg. Continued approval may depend on a confirmatory trial. Any other use, including for ageing, is off-label. As of November 1, 2026.

items.text: FDA granted accelerated approval on September 19, 2025 (NDA 215244, Stealth BioTherapeutics), with priority review and a rare pediatric disease voucher. It is a new molecular entity and a prescription drug.

src.label: FDA news release, accelerated approval of Forzinity
FDA, CDER New Drug Therapy Approvals 2025

items.text: accelerated approval rests on a measure that is “reasonably likely” to predict benefit but does not directly measure it. Here that measure is knee extensor strength. FDA requires a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial to confirm that this change means real benefit.

src.label: FDA news release, accelerated approval of Forzinity

items.text: the label says Forzinity was not better than placebo on the trial’s main goals, walk distance and fatigue.
the approval does not cover ageing, longevity, heart failure, eye disease or other mitochondrial diseases. Using it for those would be off-label.

FDA says products marketed “for research use only” or otherwise not for human consumption “have not been evaluated for safety and should never be used by humans.” “SS-31” sold this way is not Forzinity.

after.title: Sport
after.text: Elamipretide is not named on the WADA Prohibited List for 2026 or 2027. WADA’s class S0 covers only substances with no current approval by any government health regulator for human use; elamipretide has been approved in the US since September 2025. The lists do not mention it by name.

src.label: FDA news release, accelerated approval of Forzinity

after.text: Australia: Elamipretide is not named in the Poisons Standard that took effect on October 1, 2026. The TGA’s product register was not checked.

side.text: From the label: injection site reactions are the most common side effect. Serious allergic reactions have been reported. The trial data are small: 12 people with Barth syndrome.

items.text: in the 12-person controlled trial, every patient (100%) had a local reaction on elamipretide, against 67% on placebo: redness (100% vs 25%), pain (75% vs 42%), hardening (67% vs 17%), itching (67% vs 17%), bruising (25% vs 0%) and hives (25% vs 0%).

hypersensitivity reactions, including serious allergic reactions needing emergency care, have been reported. They included rash, bumps, eczema-like skin changes and cough, and can start minutes to months after starting. People with a serious reaction should not be given it again.

eosinophil counts (a type of white blood cell) often rose in studies lasting 30 days or more, peaking around day 90 and returning to baseline after 6 to 12 months or after stopping. The rise was not linked to symptoms.
the product contains benzyl alcohol, which has caused serious and fatal reactions in small and premature newborns given it by vein. Forzinity is not approved for newborns or for use by vein.
no cancer studies have been done. In rats, doses up to about 5 times human exposure did not harm fertility. There are no data in pregnant women.
the label says overdose signs are likely histamine-related, such as low blood pressure or nearly fainting.

in MMPOWER-3 (218 people), most side effects were mild to moderate. In ReCLAIM-2 (176 people), side effects were reported in 86% on elamipretide and 71% on placebo, most often injection site reactions.
Health Canada warns that unauthorized injectable peptides, a list that includes SS-31, may hold the wrong amount of ingredient or contaminants.

FDA’s orphan drug designation record for elamipretide was not checked.
UK (MHRA) status and Australia’s TGA register were not checked against the regulator’s own record.
NuPower (NCT05162768) finished in December 2024, but no results were found on the registry.
surprises: Elamipretide is marketed online as a longevity peptide, but its only approval is for Barth syndrome, and that approval came even though the pivotal trial missed both of its main goals.
The muscle strength gain behind the approval appeared only in an open-label extension without a placebo group, in 8 to 10 patients.
The one trial in healthy older adults found a short-lived rise in muscle energy after one infusion and no change in muscle fatigue.
Health Canada lists SS-31 among unauthorized injectable peptides it has seized, while the same molecule is an FDA-approved drug in the US.
